- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values.
- Underestimate mean reversion in medium-term forecasts; adjust downward when recent prices are above 75% of historical average.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., >75% above 30-day moving average); cap forecast at +15% above peak or use exponential decay to smooth.
- Lag in response to true price drops; delay forecast correction by 1–2 days for downward moves.
- Overweight recent volatility in short-term forecasts; dampen recent price momentum by applying 0.7–0.8 multiplier to recent 7-day average.
- Avoid overfitting to recent high prices; if last 5 days > 70% of 30-day average, reduce forecast by 5–10% to prevent overestimation.
- For price drops >10% from 30-day mean, apply a 2-day lagged correction to prevent premature recovery forecasts.
